title: Population settlement (rural and urban)
competency: Compare rural and urban settlements and the hierarchy of settlements.

keywords.def: A place where people live and carry out activities to make a living.
Villages and scattered homes far from towns, where people mainly farm.
Towns and cities, where people do non-agricultural work.
A very small rural settlement, usually with no services.

en.text: A settlement is a place where people live and make a living. Rural settlements are villages and scattered homes where people mainly farm. Urban settlements are towns and cities with non-farm work. From farm and hamlet up to village, town and city, size and services grow.

screens.title: Where are the services?
screens.ask: Where would you most likely find a university and an airport?
screens.after: Cities are at the top of the settlement hierarchy. They have the widest range of services.

screens.title: 2.2.5 Population settlement
paras: A settlement is a place where people live and make a living, for example by trade, farming and manufacturing.
Settlements are rural or urban, by the density of buildings and the main economic activity.

screens.title: Rural and urban
table: Villages and scattered homes far from towns

screens.text: In rural settlements, people are mainly engaged in…

screens.title: Smallest to largest settlement
screens.why: From the smallest settlement with no services to the city with the most.
Rural: farming, scattered, few people. Urban: dense, many services.

screens.text: A place has a secondary school, a bank and a health centre, but no university or airport. What level is it?
screens.why: A town has a secondary school, bank, supermarket and health centre. A city adds a university and airport.
screens.clue: Use the hierarchy table from the top down.

items.text: 1a. Style of buildings: which is typical of a city?
items.why: Urban areas have a high density of human-made structures.

items.text: 1b. Density of population: rural areas usually have…
items.why: Homesteads are isolated in rural areas.

items.text: 1c. The dominant economic activity in rural areas is…
2. Why do many people prefer to live in cities?
opts: More jobs and a wider range of goods and services
items.ans: More jobs and a wider range of goods and services
items.why: Cities offer schools, hospitals, banks and jobs.
items.clue: Look at the hierarchy of services.
